candidates.hypothesis: The stock PLA jaw faces are not parallel at wide openings and have low friction. Round objects wider than 40 mm get pushed out of the jaws, and the 514 g box slips during the last few mm of the lift.
candidates.rationale: All three failures stop the same way: stopped_by=slip, with pad_drop_t (3.46-4.46 s) showing the jaw pressure dropping under a constant command. They differ only in geometry. strawberry (width_mm=46.8) and racquetball (width_mm=55.5) are round and wider than the sphere grip limit of 40 mm. Their travel_reached (0.8435 and 0.5435 m against travel_required=0.03), contact_types=edge,pinch and peak_force of about 64-66 N mean the object was squeezed out between non-parallel faces and thrown, not lifted. The design notes say the stock faces are parallel only when closed, so wide objects are squeezed out. Tilting the pad (pad_angle_deg) makes the faces parallel at a wide opening, and a V-groove (groove_mm) centres the round objects. sugar_box (514 g) got to travel_reached=0.02447 of 0.03 before slipping, so the lift almost worked and failed on friction. A TPU skin raises friction from 0.45 to 0.9, which halves the squeeze needed to hold 5 N of weight. That is 3 edits, within the limit of max edits 3.
ruled_out: rung0: stopped_by=slip and pad_drop_t on every control, plus round objects wider than the 40 mm sphere grip (46.8 and 55.5 mm), point to a jaw geometry and friction limit. The grasp ranges (close, depth, side) that S1 already exhausted cannot change face angle or friction.
rung1: the only primitive that can lift (provides lifts=grasp) is grasp, alone or inside pick_up, so recomposing it keeps the same jaw contact that slips.
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt.
rung3: accepted_contacts=pinch only, and none of the tool templates (pad, hook, knob_cup, soft_tip, slot_inserter, probe) gives a two-jaw pinch, so only the fingers can change the pinch surfaces.

candidates.hypothesis: Non-parallel stock faces at wide openings plus PLA friction of 0.45 cause the slip. Parallel TPU pads alone should hold all three objects without a groove.
candidates.rationale: This is a fallback in case the V-groove reduces flat-face contact on sugar_box (width_mm=92.2, a box face). It keeps the two changes the evidence supports most strongly. pad_angle_deg addresses the squeeze-out seen in strawberry and racquetball: travel_reached far beyond 0.03, peak_force of about 64-66 N, contact_types including edge. pad_tpu_mm addresses the friction-limited slip of the 514 g box, which reached travel_reached=0.02447 of 0.03 before stopped_by=slip at pad_drop_t=3.46.
ruled_out: rung0: every control fails by stopped_by=slip with a pad pressure drop (pad_drop_t), which is a face-angle and friction limit that the grasp parameter ranges cannot reach.
rung1: grasp is the only lifting primitive, so any recomposed program uses the same slipping jaw contact.
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no library tool to use.
rung3: accepted_contacts=pinch, and no tool template provides a two-jaw pinch.

candidates.hypothesis: The dice (16.8 mm, 5.2 g) is narrower than the jaws can open, so aperture is not the problem. A shallow, fast pinch near the top edge, closed with the 25° tilted pads, lets the cube rotate and pop out. Gripping lower and slower at mid-height should keep it seated.
candidates.rationale: For rtr020_dice the felt evidence is stopped_by=slip with pad_drop_t=5.08: pressure was there and then dropped under a constant command, so the dice was held and then lost. peak_wrist_acc=5.903 m/s2 is the highest of the three and surprise_z peak_acc=2.742, which points to a jerky lift. peak_force=17.96 N is high for a 5.2 g part, so the jaws are squeezing it out, not gripping too weakly. The dice is well inside the widest grip (box=65 mm), ik_residual_mm=0 and joint_limit_hits=-, so reach is fine. A cheap search over depth, close timing and lift speed is the right first step.

candidates.hypothesis: The gelatin box (73 mm) and the cup (57 mm) are wider than the measured widest grip on these fingers (box=65 mm, cylinder=50 mm). The pads are only parallel near 25° of jaw opening, so at full opening the faces splay and squeeze both objects out. Tilting the pads further makes them parallel at a wider opening. A thinner TPU skin adds aperture while keeping 0.9 friction, and wider pads add contact area.
candidates.rationale: rtr000_gelatin_box has width_mm=73 against a widest box grip of 65, and rtr019_cup has width_mm=57 against a widest cylinder grip of 50. Both stopped_by=slip, with large peak_force (45.51 N and 74.82 N) and contact_types=edge,pinch. That means the jaws touched the object edge-on and pushed it out, not that they lacked squeeze. The cup lifted only payload_held_g=0.6 of its 13 g. ik_residual_mm=0 and joint_limit_hits=- rule out reach and kinematics. Past fix it000 found the same cause, non-parallel PLA faces at wide openings, and a finger change at rung 4 was accepted by mean.
ruled_out: rung0: the objects are 73 mm and 57 mm wide but the widest grips are 65 mm (box) and 50 mm (cylinder); no grasp parameter (depth, side, close) widens the jaw opening
rung1: pick_up and grasp are the only primitives that provide lifts=grasp, and both need aperture=width, so recomposing them cannot get around the aperture limit
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no library tool to use or adapt
rung3: rack tools give push, hook or edge contacts, but these objects accept only pinch, which needs both jaws, so the fix has to be the jaw pads

candidates.hypothesis: The pudding box is pinched near its top edge with little pad area, and the fast lift adds inertial load, so it slips out during the hold. A deeper, slower grasp keeps more contact area and less dynamic load.
candidates.rationale: rtr001_pudding_box reached travel_reached=0.04567 against travel_required=0.03. So the box was lifted and then lost: felt.stopped_by=slip, pad_drop_t=3.02, and payload_held_g is empty. That is a hold failure, not an approach failure. peak_force=26.69 N is the lowest of the three, and its surprise_z travel_reached=-1.353 says it lifted less than expected. A deeper grasp gives more pad contact on the 38.5 mm-tall box. A slower close and lift lowers the inertial load (peak_wrist_acc=2.914 m/s2) on the 187 g box while the jaws hold it.

candidates.hypothesis: The wide objects fail on aperture and face splay. At 25° the faces are only parallel at a moderate opening, and the 2 mm TPU plus the 3 mm groove use up opening width, so 57–90 mm objects are hit by the jaw edge and squeezed out.
candidates.rationale: Each object is wider than the measured widest grip on these fingers. gelatin_box width_mm=73 and pudding_box width_mm=89.6 are both over box=65, and cup width_mm=57 is over cylinder=50. contact_types=edge,pinch on all three shows a jaw edge landing on the object instead of a clean pinch. That matches the high peak_force (45.51, 26.69, 74.82 N) and the cup being knocked away (travel_reached=1.63, payload_held_g=0.6). it001 changed the pads more broadly (tilt, TPU and width together) and caused 2 regressions. This proposal leaves width_mm alone and changes three parameters. Each stays inside the allowed relative change. Tilting the pads further makes the faces parallel at a wider opening. A thinner TPU skin (still 0.9 friction) and a shallower groove give back aperture on each jaw.
ruled_out: rung0: widest grip (box=65, cylinder=50 mm) is below width_mm 73 and 57, and no grasp parameter widens the jaw opening
rung1: every recomposition still uses the same grasp motor, and contact_types=edge shows the jaws cannot get around the object at all
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt
rung3: the tool templates (pad, hook, knob_cup, soft_tip, slot_inserter, probe) give single-point contacts, but these objects accept only pinch, which needs both jaws

candidates.hypothesis: At 7.4 V the gripper's stall torque gives too little normal force to hold heavier boxes against gravity and lift acceleration, so they slip during the hold.
candidates.rationale: All three failures end with felt.stopped_by=slip and a pad pressure drop (pad_drop_t 3.14, 3.02, 4.22 s). The gripper runs at 7.4 V. The 187 g pudding box lifted past travel (0.04567 > 0.03) and then slipped, so squeeze force is too low even though the TPU friction is 0.9. Moving only the gripper servo to 12 V raises its stall torque and so the squeeze when the servo stalls on the object. The other joints stay as they are, which keeps the risk of regressions low.
ruled_out: rung0: grasp has no grip-force parameter, because the squeeze is set by where the servo stalls, and slip continued across the depth and speed ranges System 1 already searched (s1_exhausted)
rung1: no composition of existing primitives raises jaw normal force
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no tool to use
rung3: tool templates do not add pinch squeeze for the stock jaws
rung4: the fingers already have a 0.9-friction TPU skin, and it001's finger change still regressed, so finger geometry alone does not fix the low squeeze on heavier objects
errors: actuator is level L3, not enabled in this run (['L1'])

candidates.hypothesis: The cup is gripped near its widest rim (57 mm, wider than the 50 mm widest cylinder grip). The splayed faces touch it with a jaw edge, so it is lifted and then slips out. A deeper, slower grasp with a firmer close should catch a narrower part of the cup.
candidates.rationale: rtr019_cup was lifted: travel_reached is 1.63 against a travel_required of 0.03, and payload_held_g is 0.6. So the cup was gripped and raised, then lost during the hold (stopped_by=slip, pad_drop_t=4.22). The contact_types were edge and pinch, and the peak_force of 74.82 N is far above what a clean pad squeeze should produce. That points to a jaw edge hitting the 57 mm rim, which is wider than the 50 mm widest cylinder grip, and the cup then being squeezed out. Going deeper puts the jaws lower on the cup, where it should be narrower if it tapers like most cups. A slower descent and lift should lower the impact load (peak_wrist_acc 1.578). Closing more firmly should give a full pinch rather than an edge contact.

candidates.hypothesis: The gelatin box is wider than the widest grip these fingers can make. At 25° the pad faces are only parallel at a moderate opening, so at a 73 mm opening a jaw edge contacts the box and it is squeezed out. A modestly larger pad tilt and a slightly thinner TPU skin should allow a flat pinch on the box.
candidates.rationale: rtr000_gelatin_box is 73 mm wide and rtr001_pudding_box is 89.6 mm wide. The widest box grip measured on these fingers is 65 mm. Both runs show edge contact in contact_types, peak_force far above the 15 N tip limit (45.51 N and 26.69 N), and stopped_by=slip. That pattern means the jaw edges hit the box instead of the faces closing flat on it. Raising pad_angle_deg from 25 to 35 makes the faces parallel at a wider opening. Thinning pad_tpu_mm from 2 to 1.5 gains about 1 mm of opening while keeping the 0.9 TPU friction. it001 failed by combining a tilt, thinner TPU and wider pads, and it regressed 2 controls, so this proposal leaves width and groove unchanged to protect controls that already pass.
ruled_out: rung0: the box widths (73 and 89.6 mm) are larger than the 65 mm widest box grip, and no grasp parameter (close, depth, side, speed, lift, hold_s) changes the jaw aperture or the pad face angle
rung1: pick_up/grasp is the only primitive that provides lifts=grasp, and no recomposition of approach, contact, grasp and release widens the jaws
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt
rung3: none of the tool templates (pad, hook, knob_cup, soft_tip, slot_inserter, probe) gives a wider two-jaw pinch, and pinch is the only accepted contact for these grasp objects

candidates.hypothesis: The pudding box is actually grasped and lifted (travel_reached 0.04567 ≥ travel_required 0.03), but it slips out during the hold (stopped_by=slip, pad_drop_t=3.02). A 187 g box held by a shallow grip at full lift speed puts too much inertial and gravity load on the friction contact. A deeper grasp nearer mid-height, a firmer close, a slower lift and a shorter hold should keep it from slipping.
candidates.rationale: For rtr001_pudding_box, travel_reached=0.04567 exceeds travel_required=0.03, so the lift happens. The failure is retention (verdict=stuck, stopped_by=slip, pad_drop_t=3.02, payload_held_g=-), not aperture. Its peak_force surprise_z is -1.209 and stall_s is -0.5314, so the jaws squeezed less than usual. A firmer close (close toward the -0.17 bound) and deeper contact (depth up to 0.035) address that directly. Lowering the speed limits lift acceleration (peak_wrist_acc=2.914 m/s2). This is cheap and only narrows ranges inside the primitive bounds. It probably will not fix the gelatin box or the cup: their peak_force is 45.51 and 74.82 N and their travel_reached is 0.525 and 1.63, which means they were shoved by a jaw edge (contact_types=edge,pinch), and it003 shows a cup reparam gave delta 0.

candidates.hypothesis: The gelatin box (73 mm) and the cup (57 mm) are wider than the widest grip these fingers can take (box=65, cylinder=50 mm). So the closing jaw meets them with an edge, not a face, and shoves them away (contact_types include edge, peak_force 45–75 N, large travel_reached of 0.525 and 1.63 = pushed, not lifted). The SO-101 jaw rotates, so extending the pads past the jaw tips (reach_mm) widens the tip opening at the same jaw angle. A slightly larger pad_angle_deg then keeps the faces parallel at that wider opening. TPU friction 0.9 stays, because the pudding box needs it.
candidates.rationale: Evidence: width_mm 73 > box widest 65 and cup 57 > cylinder widest 50. peak_force=45.51/74.82 N is far above the 15 N tip cap, which is what an edge wedging against an object looks like. travel_reached=0.525 and 1.63 against travel_required=0.03 means the object was displaced, not held (payload_held_g=0.6 for the cup). Past finger edits it001 and it002 changed pad angle, TPU thickness and width; both regressed twice, partly because thinning the TPU cost friction. This proposal uses reach_mm, a lever no past edit tried, and leaves pad_tpu_mm=2 and width unchanged to limit regressions. Lowering the groove from 3 to 2 mm keeps cup centring and gives back a little aperture. pad_angle goes 25→32 (relative change 0.28), within the 1.0 limit.
ruled_out: rung0: the gelatin box and cup are wider than the measured widest grip (65/50 mm). No grasp parameter changes the jaw aperture, and it003's cup reparam gave delta 0.
rung1: every grasp program has to go through grasp/pick_up with the same stock jaws, so recombining primitives cannot widen the opening or change face splay.
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt, and pinch contact only comes from the stock jaws.
rung3: the tool templates (pad, hook, knob_cup, soft_tip, slot_inserter, probe) give single-point contacts, not a two-jaw pinch, and these controls accept only pinch.
errors: 5 parameter edits exceed the posture's max_edits 3

candidates.hypothesis: The pudding box is grasped and lifted, but it slips out during the hold. It is 187 g and held in a shallow PLA-edge pinch, and the lift acceleration overcomes the friction. A deeper grasp, a firmer close and a slower lift should give more contact area and normal force and less inertial load.
candidates.rationale: For rtr001_pudding_box, travel_reached is 0.04567, which is at least travel_required 0.03, so the lift happens. felt.stopped_by=slip and pad_drop_t=3.02 show the jaw pressure dropping during the hold. contact_types=edge,pinch shows part of the contact is on a jaw edge. peak_force 26.69 N with surprise_z peak_force -1.223 means the squeeze was lower than expected, and peak_wrist_acc is 2.914 m/s2. The iter-4 version of this idea was refused only for using 5 edits, so this proposal uses 3. ik_residual_mm=0 and joint_limit_hits=- show no reach problem.

candidates.hypothesis: The cup (57 mm at the rim) and the gelatin box (73 mm) are wider than these fingers' widest grip (cylinder 50 mm, box 65 mm). The jaws therefore catch them high up with an edge and squeeze them out. Longer pads (reach) let the grasp close lower on the tapering cup and lower on the 30 mm-tall box. A deeper V-groove centres the round cup, and more pad tilt keeps the faces parallel at the wider opening.
candidates.rationale: rtr019_cup: peak_force 74.82 N (surprise_z +1.61), payload_held_g 0.6, stopped_by=slip and contact_types=edge,pinch together point to an edge contact that squeezes the cup out instead of a face pinch. rtr000_gelatin_box: stopped_by=slip, pad_drop_t=3.14, and a wrist_roll stall_s of 1.56 point to the same squeeze-out. it003 showed that reparam depth alone gave delta 0, because the stock tips cannot go lower. it001 and it002 changed TPU thickness and width and regressed 2 controls, so this proposal leaves TPU (friction 0.9) and width alone. It uses 3 edits to stay within max_edits.
ruled_out: rung0: it003's deeper, slower, firmer grasp reparam on the cup gave delta mean 0. The objects are wider than the measured widest grip (57 > 50 mm, 73 > 65 mm), and no parameter range adds aperture or changes face splay.
rung1: no recomposition of approach, grasp, release and retreat changes the jaw geometry. pick_up already sequences grasp-lift-hold, and the failure is slip at the contact (stopped_by=slip).
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt.

rung3: these grasp controls accept only pinch (accepted_contacts=pinch), which needs both jaws. The single-contact L0 templates (pad, hook, cup, probe, edge) cannot change the jaw pads, so only a finger change helps.

candidates.hypothesis: The jaws close above each ball's equator (depth too shallow) and touch it with the jaw edge. The ball is lifted, but the inward-and-upward contact force pushes it out during the hold, so it slips.
candidates.rationale: All three balls are lifted before they are lost. travel_reached is 0.68, 1.065 and 0.944 against travel_required 0.03. felt.stopped_by=slip, and pad_drop_t is 4.0–4.76 s, during the hold. contact_types includes edge, so the jaw edge touches the ball above its equator. That squeezing geometry pushes a sphere up and out. peak_force is 44–53 N, well above what a centred pinch needs. ik_residual_mm=0 and joint_limit_hits=- show reach is not the problem. The radii are 28–37 mm, so a deeper tool point (depth near 0.035 m) puts the contact at or near the equator. A slower descent and a longer close_s let the stall settle on a centred contact.

candidates.hypothesis: At pad_angle 25° the faces are parallel only at a moderate opening. At the 55–75 mm openings these balls need, the faces splay, so a jaw edge pinches the ball off-axis and squeezes it out.
candidates.rationale: All three objects are wider than the measured widest sphere grip of 45 mm: 55.5, 66.5 and 74.6 mm. contact_types=edge,pinch together with stopped_by=slip and pad_drop_t of 4–4.8 s means the splayed faces meet each ball at an edge and it slides out. The 44–53 N peak_force shows the squeeze is wasted on a bad contact angle, not lacking in strength. Raising pad_angle_deg from 25 to 40 makes the faces parallel at the wide opening these balls need. Thinning the TPU skin from 2 to 1.5 mm gives back aperture while keeping the 0.9 friction. That is 2 edits, within max_edits 3.
ruled_out: rung0: the balls (55–75 mm) are wider than the 45 mm widest sphere grip, and grasp parameters cannot change the jaw face angle (contact_types=edge). The similar reparam it003 gave delta 0.
rung1: pick_up/grasp is the only primitive that provides lifts=grasp, so recomposing primitives cannot change the contact geometry.
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt.
rung3: the rack tool templates (pad, hook, cup, probe, slot_inserter) are not two-jaw pinch tools, and accepted_contacts=pinch requires the jaws.

candidates.hypothesis: All three balls are wider than the widest sphere grip these fingers can take (sphere=45 mm, V1 probe), and the widths are tennis_ball 66.5, racquetball 55.5 and apple 74.6 mm. At pad_angle_deg=25 the faces are only parallel at a moderate opening. At 55-75 mm they splay, so a jaw edge touches first (contact_types=edge,pinch) and squeezes the round object out of the jaws as the servo stalls. The 2 mm TPU skin on each pad also takes up opening width. If the moving pad is tilted to 40° the faces become parallel near a 60-75 mm opening. candidates.rationale: Evidence that the failure is geometric and not a matter of parameters. On every control the verdict is wrong_behavior with felt.stopped_by=slip. contact_types includes edge on all three, which is the splayed-face signature. peak_force is 52.67 / 43.84 / 44.59 N, far above the 15 N hard limit and the ball weights (41-68 g). That shows the jaws are squeezing a ball they cannot hold, not grasping weakly. The ball is ejected sideways, which loads the wrist: felt.stall_s is 2.28, 1.74 and 1.8 s, all on wrist_roll. felt.pad_drop_t is 4.0-4.76 s, so contact is lost during the lift and hold. travel_reached (0.68-1.07) is not a held lift, and payload_held_g is '-'. ik_residual_mm=0 and there are no joint_limit_hits, so reach is fine. I am changing only 2 fields, within max_edits 3. The relative changes are 0.6 and 0.5, within the limit of 1. groove_mm stays at 3 so the V-groove still centres the spheres. it006 and it002 regressed with similar ideas, so this change is more conservative: it keeps the groove and reduces the TPU skin rather than removing it.
ruled_out: rung0: every object is wider than the widest sphere grip (45 mm). Contact_types=edge and peak_force of 44-53 N, already past the 15 N limit, mean that no depth, close or speed range removes the face splay. S1 has already exhausted the grasp ranges (escalation_reason=s1_exhausted), and the similar reparams it003 and it005 gave delta mean 0
